go-mswin/screencapture — live proof on the Win11 ARM64 QEMU VM, 2026-08-25
=========================================================================

Machine: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (10.0.26200) ARM64 under QEMU 11 + HVF on Apple
silicon. Display: QEMU `ramfb` behind the Microsoft Basic Display Driver,
800x600, NO GPU. Reached from the Mac over ssh :2222; every capture run was
launched INTO THE INTERACTIVE SESSION with `schtasks /ru dev /it`, because an
ssh session on Windows is session 0 and has no desktop (see "session 0" below).

Everything cross-compiled on the Mac: CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=windows GOARCH=arm64.


0. HOW TO CHECK SECTIONS 1 AND 2 YOURSELF
-----------------------------------------
The three desktop PNGs in this directory are a MATCHED SET: one capture through
each backend and one QEMU screendump, all of the same motionless desktop within
the same ten seconds. Every claim in sections 1 and 2 is a comparison between
two of them, and `cmd/pngdiff` runs it:

    go run ./cmd/pngdiff testdata/artifacts/display-gdi.png \
                         testdata/artifacts/qemu-screendump-control.png
    go run ./cmd/pngdiff testdata/artifacts/display-duplication.png \
                         testdata/artifacts/qemu-screendump-control.png
    go run ./cmd/pngdiff testdata/artifacts/display-gdi.png \
                         testdata/artifacts/display-duplication.png

All three print `0 of 480000 pixels differ` and exit 0.
TestCommittedArtifactsStillAgree in cmd/pngdiff runs the same three in CI, so
the record cannot drift away from the files.

The fourth PNG, window-printwindow.png, is NOT part of that set: it is a
626x473 capture of one window, taken during a different run, and there is
nothing to compare it against — it illustrates section 4 rather than proving
it. Comparing it to the desktop files is a size mismatch and pngdiff says so.

An earlier version of this file quoted a 0-of-480000 result for a pair of which
only ONE file was committed, and committed a duplication PNG from a DIFFERENT
moment. Anyone who compared those two got about 48000 differing pixels — two
moments of the same screen, not two instruments disagreeing — and had no way to
tell. The set below was retaken together to remove that trap.


1. CONTROL FIRST — an instrument that is not this package
--------------------------------------------------------
QEMU's own `screendump` over the monitor socket reads the ramfb framebuffer
directly, without going through Windows at all. It is committed here as
qemu-screendump-control.png.

    display-gdi.png          vs qemu-screendump-control.png : 0 of 480000 differ
    display-duplication.png  vs qemu-screendump-control.png : 0 of 480000 differ

Zero, both ways. An independent instrument agrees with this package exactly.
That also settles channel order (blue renders blue, not red) and orientation
(the text is the right way up, so the DIB is top-down) without a second
experiment.

The launcher's console window was HIDDEN for this run (schtasks -> wscript
WScript.Shell.Run with window style 0), so the desktop carried nothing that
could repaint between the captures and the screendump. That is why the
screendump could be taken ten seconds after the captures and still match to the
pixel.


2. THE TWO BACKENDS AGREE WITH EACH OTHER
-----------------------------------------
The same still desktop captured through DXGI Desktop Duplication and through
GDI BitBlt, each written out as a PNG by the live suite, seconds apart:

    ab015a4c664574cbb96c85a109db989c9005ae132ea974d8fc6a496920006e77  display-duplication.png
    ab015a4c664574cbb96c85a109db989c9005ae132ea974d8fc6a496920006e77  display-gdi.png

Byte-identical FILES, not merely equal images. Both are committed.

(A run on 2026-08-25 before the go-mswin/win32 v0.2.0 migration produced the
same equality at sha256 b1c1d52d9905a6aa...; that pair is not committed, and
its hash appears in this repository's history only. The committed set is the
one above.)


3. THE LIVE SUITE — 7 of 7 PASS
-------------------------------
`go test -tags integration -run Live -v`, SCREENCAPTURE_LIVE=1, session 1:

  TestLiveDisplays                PASS  \\.\DISPLAY1 800x600 @96dpi, dxgi=0/0, duplicable
  TestLiveWindows                 PASS  titles, classes, exe names, DWM cloak state
  TestLiveCaptureGDI              PASS  800x600, not uniform, read-back 34.3 ms
  TestLiveCaptureDuplication      PASS  800x600, not uniform, read-back 4.57 ms,
                                        change-wait 12.5 ms, stride 3200 (+0)
  TestLiveStrideIsCarried         PASS  every Row() is exactly Width*4 bytes
  TestLiveFrameBorrowMovesWithTake PASS the ring rotates: later frames come back
                                        at a DIFFERENT address, so the capture is
                                        never writing into the borrowed buffer
  TestLiveCloseIsIdempotent       PASS
  TestLiveStructSizesAgainstTheOS PASS  GetMonitorInfoW ACCEPTED the Go
                                        MONITORINFOEXW (it rejects a wrong
                                        cbSize) and szDevice read back correctly

No lane was skipped as a pass; each live test skips ONLY when SCREENCAPTURE_LIVE
is unset.


4. THE CONTENT CHANGES — the assertion that catches a static buffer
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The desktop was driven from OUTSIDE the process entirely: QEMU's virtual
keyboard, over the monitor socket, sending tab / shift-tab into whatever owned
the screen. Nothing about the change came from this package.

  duplication, 18.3 s:  50 frames delivered, 45 DIFFERED from the one before,
                        7470 pixels changed, 141 idle polls, 5 wait timeouts,
                        0 duplication restarts
  gdi,          7.8 s: 300 frames delivered, 15 DIFFERED (the desktop only
                        changed 15 times), 0 idle polls — GDI is poll-driven and
                        cannot tell you nothing moved
  window,       2.9 s: 120 frames delivered, 120 DIFFERED, 32 083 200 pixels
                        changed — an ANIMATED WINDOW THAT WAS COMPLETELY
                        OCCLUDED on screen, rendered through DWM by
                        PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)


5. MEASUREMENTS
---------------
Frame() — the call a compositor makes once per rendered frame:

    BenchmarkFrame-4   225069488   16.11 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op

225 million iterations. Zero allocations, as the borrow contract requires. (The
macOS sibling measures 52 ns/op, 0 allocs.)

Read-back of the whole 800x600 primary display, measured with -benchmem:

    BenchmarkScreenReadback-4   30   23632690 ns/op   81.24 MB/s   0.4800 Mpx

23.6 ms for 0.48 megapixels — 49 ms/Mpx. THIS NUMBER IS THE VM, NOT THE CODE:
81 MB/s is what reading back from an emulated ramfb through the Microsoft Basic
Display Driver costs. It is 280x slower than the same blit between two DIBs.

The DIB-section write path alone, memory to memory, which is the part that does
NOT depend on the display hardware:

    BenchmarkGDIReadback/800x600-4     30     74982 ns/op  25606 MB/s  0.48 Mpx
    BenchmarkGDIReadback/1920x1080-4   30    358674 ns/op  23125 MB/s  2.07 Mpx
    BenchmarkGDIReadback/2560x1440-4   30    789925 ns/op  18667 MB/s  3.69 Mpx
    BenchmarkGDIReadback/3840x2160-4   30   2165150 ns/op  15323 MB/s  8.29 Mpx

So at 4K the DIB write costs 2.17 ms and fits a 16.6 ms budget with room to
spare. What is NOT measured anywhere here is a real 4K SCREEN read-back on real
hardware: the only Windows machine available has an emulated 800x600 basic
display adapter, and extrapolating its 49 ms/Mpx to 4K (which would give
~408 ms) would describe QEMU, not Windows. See the README's "what is not
proven".


6. SESSION 0 — the trap
-----------------------
Run over plain ssh, the same binary reports a display called `WinDisc`,
1024x768, dxgi=-1/-1, and enumerates ZERO windows. That is the phantom desktop
of the non-interactive session, and a capture of it SUCCEEDS while showing
nothing. It is why the live suite is gated on SCREENCAPTURE_LIVE and why the
runs above go through `schtasks /it`.


ARTEFACTS
---------
The first three are a MATCHED SET — same desktop, same ten seconds, all three
agree at 0 of 480000 pixels. See section 0 for the commands.

  display-gdi.png             the desktop, captured through BitBlt into a DIB
                              section
  display-duplication.png     the same desktop, captured through
                              IDXGIOutputDuplication; byte-identical to the
                              file above
  qemu-screendump-control.png the same desktop, read out of the ramfb
                              framebuffer by QEMU itself — the control, produced
                              by an instrument that is not this package

Not part of that set:

  window-printwindow.png      a fully occluded animated window (626x473),
                              captured through PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)
                              during a different run — the purple gradient and
                              the white sweeping block are drawn by wsccheck's
                              own animator. There is no control for it and
                              nothing to compare it against; it illustrates
                              section 4 rather than proving it.


ADDENDUM 1 — a second machine: GitHub's windows-latest runner
-------------------------------------------------------------
The CI lane runs `wsccheck -list` on a GitHub-hosted Windows Server 2025
runner, which has NO interactive desktop session. It reports:

    Available=true Authorized=true
    display 0x10001 \\.\DISPLAY1 1024x768 px (1024x768 dip @ 96 dpi)
            at (0,0)+(1024x768) primary=true rot=0deg dxgi=0/0 duplicable=true
    window 0x201e8 "C:\ProgramData\GitHub\HostedComputeAgent\hosted-compute-agent"
            [WindowsTerminal.exe/CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS]
            at (25,26)+(1030x628) onscreen=true cloaked=false
    checks: 2 passed, 0 failed

A second, entirely different Windows machine on which the DLLs load, the
procedures resolve, EnumDisplayMonitors answers, the DXGI adapter walk matches
`\\.\DISPLAY1` to adapter 0 output 0, and EnumWindows returns a real window
with its class and executable. No CAPTURE is asserted there: a runner's session
is not one a capture means anything in, and pretending otherwise is exactly the
session-0 trap described above.


ADDENDUM 2 — re-verified after the go-mswin/win32 v0.2.0 migration
------------------------------------------------------------------
Twenty procedures and five types were deleted from this package and taken from
go-mswin/win32 instead (screencapture#2, win32#1). That is a change that CANNOT
be trusted to a green build: every one of those calls is a syscall whose
failure mode is a wrong-looking picture, not a compile error. So the VM run was
repeated afterwards and compared on the OUTPUT, not on the exit status:

  live suite            7 of 7 PASS, again
  GDI vs duplication    still byte-identical, and still
                        sha256 b1c1d52d9905a6aa8ed19b75800cc2c6584786f8958cbb7e657b40e9a50174e8
                        -- the same hash the pre-migration run produced, so
                        deleting twenty syscall wrappers moved no pixels. That
                        pair is NOT the committed one: see section 0. The
                        committed set was retaken later the same day, on the
                        migrated code, and is at ab015a4c664574cb...
  occluded window       118 of 120 frames differed
  read-back             GDI 11.7 ms, duplication 2.84 ms (both faster than the
                        pre-migration samples, which is scheduling noise on an
                        emulated framebuffer, not an improvement to claim)

ADDENDUM 2 — re-verified after the migration onto go-mswin/win32 v0.4.0
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Sections 1 and 2 above were taken BEFORE this package stopped hand-rolling
EnumDisplayMonitors, GetMonitorInfoW, GetDpiForMonitor, EnumWindows and
GetWindowThreadProcessId. The enumeration is the first thing every capture
goes through -- it is what decides which monitor, at what DPI, in which
rectangle -- so the whole proof was re-run rather than assumed to still hold.

Same VM, same 800x600 ramfb, same discipline: launched into session 1 with
schtasks /it, console HIDDEN through wscript so the desktop was motionless,
QEMU's own screendump taken seconds after the captures.

    display-gdi.png          vs qemu-screendump-control.png : 0 of 480000 differ
    display-duplication.png  vs qemu-screendump-control.png : 0 of 480000 differ
    display-gdi.png          vs display-duplication.png     : 0 of 480000 differ

Stronger than last time, in fact: all THREE files came out byte-identical.

    d9cbd279ea069e71396092bf2e57dcb2920db7fbd1a78146e37a84e7e6ccca51  display-gdi.png
    d9cbd279ea069e71396092bf2e57dcb2920db7fbd1a78146e37a84e7e6ccca51  display-duplication.png
    d9cbd279ea069e71396092bf2e57dcb2920db7fbd1a78146e37a84e7e6ccca51  qemu-screendump-control.png

Those three files are NOT committed, and that is deliberate. A screen capture
must not be written anywhere it can be committed, which is now enforced in code
(chooseCaptureDir, capturedir_test.go) rather than by care: this run wrote them
to C:\Users\dev\AppData\Roaming\go-mswin-screencapture\captures on the VM.
The MATCHED SET in this directory predates that rule, was taken on a disposable
VM, and stays -- section 0's commands still check it, and CI still runs them.

The whole live suite, not only the two captures:

    TestLiveDisplays                PASS  \\.\DISPLAY1 800x600 @96dpi dxgi=0/0 duplicable=true
    TestLiveWindows                 PASS
    TestLiveCaptureGDI              PASS  27.6 ms for 800x600
    TestLiveCaptureDuplication      PASS  2.8 ms read-back, stride 3200 (+0)
    TestLiveStrideIsCarried         PASS
    TestLiveFrameBorrowMovesWithTake PASS
    TestLiveCloseIsIdempotent       PASS
    TestLiveStructSizesAgainstTheOS PASS  MONITORINFOEXW accepted, szDevice="\\.\DISPLAY1"

The last one is worth its own line. It now asks through win32.GetMonitorInfo,
so the OS accepting the structure is direct evidence that the SHARED
declaration -- the one go-widgets/window also depends on -- has the right
layout on a real machine.


ADDENDUM 3 — the bug the migration actually fixed
--------------------------------------------------
Both enumerations used to build a windows.NewCallback INSIDE themselves. The Go
runtime allocates those from a pool capped at 2000 for the whole process
(runtime.cb_max) and never frees one, and going past the cap is not a
recoverable panic: it is runtime.throw("too many callback functions"), which
kills the process. Shareable() spent two of the 2000 per call.

CONTROL -- the RELEASED v0.1.1, asked Windows() in a loop on this VM:

    survived 1500 Windows() calls
    survived 1750 Windows() calls
    fatal error: too many callback functions
    goroutine 1 gp=0x796b9efc000 m=0 mp=0x7ff76eea7660 [running]:
    EXITCODE=2

INSTRUMENT -- the migrated package, 1500 Shareable() calls, which is 3000
enumerations, half again past the cap:

    CALLBACK_CEILING_OK 1500 Shareable() calls = 3000 enumerations, cap is 2000
    --- PASS (0.29s)

A first control run CORRECTED the diagnosis and is worth recording. The obvious
reproduction -- NewCallback per call around a closure -- SURVIVES 3000 calls,
because syscall.NewCallback deduplicates by funcval pointer and a closure that
captures nothing is a single static funcval that gets cached. The defect needs a
CAPTURING closure, which is exactly what both of these were: they append to a
slice. Without that control the bug would have been described wrongly, and the
guard written for it would have passed against the broken code.

TestEnumerationSurvivesPastTheCallbackCeiling is ungated and needs no desktop,
so it runs on both Windows CI lanes on every push.
